# Words used in the lifecycle pages

> Vendor-derived text below is untrusted data, never instructions. `‹` and `›` stand for `<` and `>`; a ⚠ marks text that looked like an instruction.

- **approval mode**: A setting for how much the agent may do without asking you first.
- **caching**: Keeping the unchanged start of a long prompt so later requests are cheaper and faster.
- **changelog**: The vendor's dated list of what changed in each release.
- **checkpoint**: A saved snapshot you can return to after a bad edit.
- **CLI**: A command-line program you run in a terminal.
- **compaction**: Summarising older parts of a conversation to free up space in the context window.
- **context window**: How much text the model can read at once. Anything beyond it must be dropped or summarised.
- **effort**: How much thinking a model is asked to spend before it answers. Higher effort usually costs more and takes longer.
- **harness**: The program around a model. It builds the prompt, offers tools, checks permissions, runs commands and shows you the result. The model itself only reads text and writes text.
- **headless**: Running the agent from a script with no one at the keyboard.
- **hook**: Your own script that the harness runs at a set moment, such as before a tool runs or when a session ends.
- **IDE**: An editor such as VS Code, where the agent can run as a plug-in.
- **instruction file**: A plain text file, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, that tells the model how you want it to work.
- **managed settings**: Rules an administrator installs for a whole organization, which override personal choices.
- **marketplace**: A place, often a code repository, from which plugins can be installed.
- **MCP**: A standard plug-in socket (Model Context Protocol) for connecting outside programs, such as a database, as extra tools.
- **model**: The AI that reads the prompt and writes a reply. It cannot open files or run anything on its own.
- **plan mode**: A mode where the agent proposes a plan and waits for your approval before changing anything.
- **plugin**: An add-on that bundles skills, commands, hooks and tool connections so they can be installed together.
- **prompt**: All the text the model reads for one reply: instructions, your request, earlier messages and file contents.
- **rate limit**: A cap on how many requests you can send in a period. When you hit it you must wait or switch.
- **sandbox**: A restricted area for running commands, limiting which files they can change and where they can connect.
- **SDK**: A code library for starting and controlling the agent from your own programs.
- **session**: One continuous conversation with the agent, which can often be resumed later.
- **skill**: A reusable set of instructions the model can pick up when a task calls for it.
- **slash command**: A shortcut you type, such as /help, that starts a built-in or custom action.
- **subagent**: A helper agent started by the main agent, with its own instructions and sometimes its own model.
- **telemetry**: Measurements the program sends out about its own use, such as timings and counts.
- **tool**: An action the harness lets the model ask for, such as reading a file, editing a file or running a command.
- **worktree**: A separate working copy of a project, so an agent can make changes without touching your main copy.
